about: The kinds of system a ship graph is made of (docs/ship-graph.md). A system names its type; what's here is what every system of that type is, so a design only says what's different. role: bus (carries a resource between systems), source (puts a resource in), store (takes and gives back), conduit (a path power runs through), load (uses it), group (holds others: no flow of its own). Resources: power, eps, odn, deu, am, heat. lastResort: a source drawn on only when nothing else will do (batteries, the EPS's pressure).

bus.about: A low-power bus (A, B, C): a pool its sources feed and its loads draw from.

eps-manifold.about: The EPS: high-energy plasma, from the reactors to the big loads and down the taps to the low buses.

solar.about: Solar arrays: their output, while tied.

emergency-battery.about: A consumable battery: supplies its bus when nothing else will, never recharged aboard (replaced at a starbase).

battery.about: A bus battery: charges from its bus, covers a shortfall; its main breaker in or out of service.

eps-pressure.about: The EPS manifold's own charge: pressure it holds and gives back.

fusion-reactor.about: An impulse or auxiliary fusion reactor: deuterium in, EPS out; its chamber is a subsystem on the low buses.

thrusters.about: A drive's maneuvering thrusters: tied to the EPS, what the drive isn't spending on thrust feeds it.

warp-core.about: The matter/antimatter reaction: deuterium and antimatter in, EPS out; constriction, injector and antimatter conduit are its subsystems.

dock-feed.about: Power through the docking connectors: a starbase's, or a docked ship's (import and export).

docking-port.about: A docking port: everything a connection carries. count: null on a starbase, as many as are needed.

docking-connectors.about: The connectors behind the ports, where a connection's resources come aboard.

fuel-bus.about: The deuterium or antimatter bus: moves fuel between the tanks and what burns it.

tank.about: Fuel storage: the main tanks or pods, or a system's own tank.

place.about: A place aboard (a deck's room): the conduit its loads' power runs through, tied to the buses it may carry.

conduit.about: A path power runs through below a place (life support's, for its systems).

group.about: A heading over systems that have no flow of their own together (the computer cores).

console.about: A station's console: dark without power.

system.about: A ship system (shields, sensors, transporter...): draws its rating at 100%.

subsystem.about: Part of a system, a station or a source: its parent stops without it.

containment.about: Antimatter containment: the pods', or a tank's own; never let go with antimatter in it.

coolant-loop.about: Coolant: carries heat from the systems that make it to the heat sinks and radiators.

heat-sink.about: Takes heat faster than the radiators can dump it, and gives it back to them: time, not a way out.

radiator.about: Dumps heat to space at its rate; its coolant pumps run on power.

export.about: Power sent out through the docking connectors: to the starbase, or to a ship docked at a port.

heat.about: Heat (step 2 simulates it): what a system makes, as a share of what it handles. of: "consumes" (a load's draw) or "produces" (a source's output). byEffect: a hotter share for what a system does. A system whose heat can't leave warms: past warm, its effects weaken; past hot, it takes damage.

temperature.about: Of a system's heat limit (step 2): above warm it works less well, above hot it's damaged.
